note:
v1 92.522/92.512. THE TRITONE QUESTION: afro-tinged minimal house, 119 -> 119.5 bpm, B minor.
- The hook is the TRITONE PARADOX: Shepard-tone pairs a tritone apart, B-F first, then each stair step with its tritone (B-F, C#-G, D-G#, F#-C). The stair climbs, but every step has no up or down.
- A voice asks it aloud once the seam has passed: "up... or down?", answering t3's "one more step up".
- A 12/8 bell and triplet tom pickups over the four on the floor; triplet shakers, sixteenths at the peak; a clap a triplet late.
- The machine boom as a bass line on B; a sparse Bm9 dub stab in an echo room.
- A kickless break with the question slowed.
- SEAMS: in, a BASS SWAP: t4's first 16 bars have a high-passed kick so t3 keeps the low end, and its shakers and hats sit under t3's phrase. Out: kick, hats and a held B1 for t5's 808 (mixplan rows filled).
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: Rhythm (57: the triplets read as on-grid); ears on the pairs' level.

note:
v4 88.252/88.572 (v3 rescored 91.052/89.993; kept on judgment for Harry's 31 Oct steers: illusions in front all the way through, much more time-play, darker).
THE QUESTION IN TIME (T4_R4). Two Risset rhythms against the steady kick: bright toms and bell accelerating for ever on the left, dark toms and rim decelerating for ever on the right. Different registers keep them two streams on speakers. The groove itself now asks "up or down?". Each section has its own time:
- A1 slowing, A2 speeding, the break slowing alone, the drops speeding into the peak.
- B2 both at once, where the answer is both.
- Hints of the slowing stream in both seams.
The tritone pairs are back in front (every bar, -8 dB). The stab goes darker: every fourth bar the Bm9 shape planes up a semitone over the B pedal (a Phrygian b2 rub).
Illusion meter: -7.7 LU / 40% / 46 s gaps -> -3.7 LU / 75% / 31 s. The gaps left are the two seam windows, where t3's and t5's illusions overlap.
compscore: variety falls (percussive Risset hits even out the onset density, 0.24 -> 0.13); sparser loops, a 4 dB trim and per-section directions recovered part of it.
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. Recipes in sounds.md for the closer. (Not queued.)
next: Variety (onset density evened by the Rissets); the seam windows' illusion hints.

note: v5 88.706/89.072 (v4 rescored 88.253/88.572). 3:2 (T4_R5), on wM's time-play part 1 (e5c3171c). The Risset copies of both time streams (the bright toms speeding up for ever, the dark toms slowing for ever) now sit a metric modulation apart, 3:2, instead of an octave of tempo. Each step of the endless acceleration or slowing is the 12/8-against-4 hemiola the bell and the dotted-quarter toms already play, so the question in time speaks t4's own cross-rhythm. note: v6 88.939/89.263 (v5 rescored 88.706/89.072). THE RISER (T4_R6), on wM's time-play part 2. Each 4-bar drop's noise rise becomes the endless Shepard riser (fx-riser-endless, swell over the drop, tinted B). It climbs for ever over the accelerating 3:2 Risset toms and stops dead on the groove's return: pitch and time both rising at once into each groove. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v7 88.859/89.234 (v6 rescored 88.956/89.276; kept on judgment: a big pass on Harry's third steer, near parity) (T4_R7=phantom).
- PHANTOM WORDS: the exposed spoken "up... or down?" is gone. Two voices, hard left and right, repeat "up" and "down" on a dotted-eighth grid, each a syllable behind the other: at every moment one side says "up" and the other "down". This is Deutsch's phantom words, and it works on speakers.
- SPEECH TO SONG: from the break's third bar the syllables' speech contours flatten bar by bar until "up" is sung on B and "down" on F, so the words become the tritone question again. They return, sung and quieter, under the peak's last 12 bars.
- THE FORM is no longer 4/8/16: A1 22, A2 10, break 14, B1 6, B2 32.
- THE CHORD MUTATES: Bm9 in A1, Bm11 in A2, G6/9#11 over the B pedal in B1. In B2 it turns every three bars through Bm9, Gmaj9#11/B and Em9/B.
- The break's slowing Risset is gone: the words are its rhythm now. Bringing the words in from bar 0 flattened variety (density cv 0.09, 87.8); from bar 4 the break split and recurrence fell (87.9); bar 2 balances both.
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 2. (Not queued.)
next: Variety; a spiral into a key change?

note:
v8 89.758/89.932 (v7 rescored 88.861/89.235). HUMAN PHANTOM WORDS (T4_R8), on wM's voice tools.
- The phantom syllables are a human voice now: chirp tts "up down" --humanize 0.6 --repeat 12 --melodize 1 --melody "B2 F2" (the JSON is committed next to the generator).
- Each of the break's twelve phantom bars takes one repetition: its pitch, the syllable's own f0 path (stress, a rise and fall, the end falling) and its effort. So the words drift and wobble like real speech, then settle onto B and F as song, with real speech-to-song in place of my flattened contours. The peak's return takes the last, sung repetition.
- Same phantom grid as v7: left and right a syllable apart on dotted eighths.
- At -16 dB, under the break: the human voice is louder than the old one (at -10 dB it cost 4 points of variety and recurrence).
-11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
next: A radio or vocoder on the phantom voices? Flow (52).

note:
v9 89.526/89.682 (v8 rescored 89.719/89.893; kept on judgment: a structural modulation-and-spiral pass, -0.2). THE KEY FLIP (T4_R9=flip): the peak asks the tritone question in KEYS.
- B2 (32 bars) is 12 bars in B minor, then a 4-bar TURN: bass and stab gone, and a pluck Shepard-Risset spiral of the stair (risset pitch: true) climbing over the drums and the Shepard tritone pairs.
- Then 12 bars a TRITONE away in F minor (bass, stab and pairs all moved six semitones). The phantom words return here, sung, so their "down" on F is now home and "up" on B the stranger.
- Then another 4-bar spiral (F G Ab C), and the out seam back in B minor.
A tritone is the same distance up as down: did the key climb or fall? It moved twice and is home. Spectrum 92.2 -> 94.0; variety 86.7 -> 84.6. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)

v10 88.266/88.28 (v9 rescored on the novelty ensemble 87.088/86.527). THE FLOOR TILTS (T4_R10=hemi): a metric modulation in place of the plainest stretch.
- A1 was 22 bars of one groove. It is now 12, then a NEW 10-bar section where the kick and the bass (B B F# D) move onto the dotted quarter, every 1.5 beats across the bar lines.
- Meanwhile the 12/8 bell, all twelve triplet hats and the tritone pairs keep the old grid, and open hats mark the new pulse's off-beats.
- The floor seems to slow to two thirds of the tempo while nothing has slowed. The four returns with the drop's riser.
- A1's slowing Risset now ends where the section begins.
The form is no longer borderline: the ensemble finds 6-8 sections at most cuts (was 5-7). Variety 80.8 -> 83.8, recurrence 84.5 -> 88.4, spectrum 94.0 -> 94.9. -11.0 LUFS, TP -1.29, run 1. (Not queued.)
